summary:
I checked the EndingObeysSkip mutant itself on this machine, and all nine acceptance criteria hold.
- **Real run:** `WindowMutants.ps1 -Mutant EndingObeysSkip` exited 0 in 51 s. It published the mutated app in a scratch copy, and L-002 failed on topLevel.final 'False'. The secondary figures this time were bytes 327680 and files 5, not the builder's 393216 and 6. That supports the MayFail allowance: those symptoms vary from run to run, and only the final line is constant.
- **Full suite:** `-Mutant All` exited 0 in 333 s, with all 9 mutants killed.
- **Unmutated control:** C-008 exited 0. L-002 passed with the skip armed, run through the harness's own New-Scratch and Invoke-ScratchCase.
- **O-010 (owed to this stage) is discharged.** I sent two real broken mutations through the real Test-CaseMutant:
  - a compile error (CS0103, publish failed) was counted NOT killed;
  - a crash at the ending (exit code fails, no report written) was counted NOT killed.

The verdict is `partial`, not `passes`, because O-011 is still open. It is a fix owed to build-slice, and the tree does not have it. The C-007 case in tests/bugs/SL-064-MutantCases.ps1 still decides whether its scratch copy was cleaned up by comparing two listings of the shared %TEMP%\fsa-window-mutants folder (lines 354 and 367-368). I reproduced the false failure the natural way: I started C-008 10 s after C-007. Every real check in C-007 passed, and its own copy (cb024f63…) was removed. It still went red on C-008's copy (a5879e2e…), and exited 1. The slice should go back to build-slice for that fix alone.

This is not a loop: there was one build attempt and one review attempt. The bug report was only a title. I took the intended fix to be a standing mutant in the test harness with no app change, and the diff matches that: only tests/ and .taad/ changed. No scratch copies or FsAnalyser.App processes were left behind, my temp folder was removed, and the working tree is unchanged.

checks.evidence: 61 rules checked against 99 parsed files: every declared rule holds.

checks.what: C-001: -Mutant EndingObeysSkip binds through the real param block; an unlisted name is refused
checks.evidence: exit 0. Bound EndingObeysSkip. All still binds. 'EndingObeysSkipX' is refused with ParameterBindingValidationException.

checks.what: C-002: the $CaseMutants entry is wired to L-002 and MainWindow.xaml.cs, and the run loop routes it to Test-CaseMutant
checks.evidence: exit 0. Case L-002, File src\FsAnalyser.App\MainWindow.xaml.cs (exists), Test-L002 defined, no Test-EndingObeysSkip.

checks.what: C-003: the anchor matches once, inside ShowFinalTopLevel; Set-Mutation refuses the anchor twice or reformatted
checks.evidence: exit 0. 1 match at offset 15197, method spans 15067-15515. Text before and after the method is unchanged, and the method now has '&& !_skipNextRefresh'. Anchor twice: 'matches 2 times', refused. Reformatted: 'matches 0 times', refused. The file is left alone in both.

checks.what: C-004: the real and mutated guard compiled; with the skip armed the real one shows the final snapshot and the mutant does not
checks.evidence: exit 0. Real: shown 1 with the skip armed. Mutant: shown 0 with the skip armed, and the earlier snapshot is kept. Both show the final snapshot with no skip, and both clear on null.

checks.what: C-005: Test-CaseMutant's classification over synthetic L-002 outputs
checks.evidence: exit 0. All 8 shapes classified as expected. Killed: the full signature, and final alone. Not killed: L-002 passed, final held, final <null>, hook never acted, crash, publish failed.

checks.what: C-006: the -Mutant All roster contains EndingObeysSkip and every ValidateSet name, each once
checks.evidence: exit 0. Roster: StopDisabled, StopCollapsed, NoCrashHandler, NoExitRule, CancelThrows, HookFailsAfterActing, HookCompileError, HookLocked, EndingObeysSkip. None missing, no duplicates.

checks.what: O-010 / criteria 5, 7: real end-to-end mutant run through the standing harness
checks.evidence: exit 0 in 51 s. The hook was built and the mutated app published in %TEMP%\fsa-window-mutants\caa892d5…. L-002: hook watch armed=True, then FAIL reading 0/1, bytes 524288/327680, files 8/5, final 'True'/'False', then FAILED: L-002. Harness: 'failed on /topLevel.final…/ and nothing else besides /topLevel.(reading|bytes|files)…/ (got 1)', and 'the run shows actual False'. PASSED: EndingObeysSkip. MainWindow.xaml.cs hash unchanged, 0 scratch copies left, 0 app processes.

checks.what: O-010 / criterion 9: a real compile-error mutation through the real Test-CaseMutant is not counted as killed
checks.command: Temp driver in %TEMP%\sl064-validate (since deleted). It loaded WindowMutants.ps1's pre-$names statements as a module (the same way New-Harness does), ran Use-RepoSdk, set $CaseMutants['EndingObeysSkip'].Replace to reference '_noSuchFieldValidate', and ran Test-CaseMutant.
checks.evidence: Publish failed: MainWindow.xaml.cs(338,62): error CS0103: The name '_noSuchFieldValidate' does not exist; publish failed with exit 1. Harness: FAIL 'L-002 is reported FAILED', FAIL 'failed on /topLevel.final/ … (got 0)', FAIL 'the run shows actual False'. Counted NOT killed.

checks.what: O-010 / criterion 9: a real crash at the ending through the real Test-CaseMutant is not counted as killed
checks.command: Same driver, with Replace = 'else if (_skipNextRefresh ? throw new InvalidOperationException(...) : !ReferenceEquals(final, _shownTopLevel))'
checks.evidence: The app published and the hook acted with armed=True. L-002: FAIL exit code, FAIL a report was written, FAILED: L-002. Harness: 'failed on /topLevel.final/ … (got 2: FAIL exit code | FAIL a report was written)', and 'the run shows actual False' also failed. Counted NOT killed. Source hash unchanged, 0 scratch copies left, 0 app processes.

checks.what: Criterion 8: L-002 against an unmutated copy made by the harness's own New-Scratch and Invoke-ScratchCase
checks.evidence: exit 0 in 51 s. The copy's hash equals the real source. L-002 PASSED with no FAIL line, skip armed, and topLevel.final held. Remove-Scratch removed the copy, and the real source is unchanged.

checks.what: O-011 reproduction: C-007 run while another harness user (C-008, started 10 s later) holds a scratch copy in the shared folder
checks.command: Start-Process pwsh … SL-064-MutantCases.ps1 -Case C-007; after 10 s Start-Process pwsh … -Case C-008; wait for both
checks.evidence: C-007 exit 1, C-008 exit 0, 67 s. All 9 substantive C-007 checks passed: exit 0, PASSED, published, armed, the final FAIL line, 'False', FAILED L-002, matched, source unchanged. Then: 'FAIL the scratch copy was removed (…\fsa-window-mutants\a5879e2ed00a467c976b0ebd874477ff)'. That GUID appears 7 times in C-008's output and never in C-007's. C-007's own copy, cb024f63422a407d883a00d10b261176, no longer exists. This is a false red: exactly the defect O-011 describes, still in the tree at SL-064-MutantCases.ps1:354 and :367-368.

checks.what: Criterion 6: full mutant suite, as normally scheduled
checks.evidence: exit 0 in 333 s. PASSED: StopDisabled, StopCollapsed, NoCrashHandler, NoExitRule, CancelThrows, HookFailsAfterActing, HookCompileError, HookLocked, EndingObeysSkip. Each of the 8 older mutants still matched its own exact Fail list with no MayFail. 0 scratch copies left, 0 app processes.

checks.what: Both changed scripts parse under Windows PowerShell 5.1 and pwsh 7, and are pure ASCII
checks.command: powershell.exe and pwsh Parser::ParseFile on tests/window/WindowMutants.ps1 and tests/bugs/SL-064-MutantCases.ps1, plus a byte scan for values > 127
checks.evidence: 0 parse errors in both editions for both files; 0 non-ASCII bytes.

checks.what: Environment: the repo-local SDK is present and no leftovers remain before or after
checks.evidence: SDK 10.0.401 in the worktree's gitignored .dotnet (per Q-003). The scratch parent is empty before and after every run, and there are no FsAnalyser.App processes. git status shows only the pre-existing .taad changes. %TEMP%\sl064-validate was removed.
Not re-run by design. The engine ran it and recorded exit 0 (O-001 discharged).

checks.what: C-007 run alone, with nothing else using the scratch folder
checks.evidence: Not run in isolation by me. Builder and reviewer both report exit 0. My concurrent run showed every substantive C-007 check passing, and my standalone -Mutant EndingObeysSkip run covers the same path.

checks.what: dotnet build / dotnet test of FsAnalyser.slnx
checks.evidence: No src/ or C# test file changed (git diff aa225be..HEAD touches only tests/*.ps1 and .taad/). The app was built only inside the harness's scratch copies, 6 successful publishes and 1 deliberate failure.

criteria.criterion: 1. invoke the mutant harness by name, when -Mutant EndingObeysSkip is passed as the parameter value
criteria.how: The real run of WindowMutants.ps1 -Mutant EndingObeysSkip bound and exited 0. C-001 exits 0: it binds through the real param block and an unlisted name is refused.

criteria.criterion: 2. look up which case and file a mutant targets, when $CaseMutants is queried by the key 'EndingObeysSkip'
criteria.how: C-002 exits 0 (Case L-002, File MainWindow.xaml.cs). The real run mutated the scratch copy's MainWindow.xaml.cs (the compile-error variant's CS0103 points at MainWindow.xaml.cs:338) and ran L-002.

criteria.criterion: 3. apply the mutant's Find/Replace to the real source, when the Find anchor matches exactly once in the current file
criteria.how: C-003 exits 0: 1 match, inside ShowFinalTopLevel (15197 within 15067-15515). Duplicated and reformatted anchors are refused. The real run applied it: Set-Mutation would have thrown otherwise, and the published app behaved as the mutant.

criteria.criterion: 4. the mutated guard decides whether to show the final snapshot, when _skipNextRefresh is true at the scan's end
criteria.how: C-004 compiles both guards: the real one shows the final snapshot with the skip armed, the mutant does not. In the real run the hook logged armed=True and the report's topLevel.final was False; in the unmutated control it was True.

criteria.criterion: 5. the harness decides whether a mutant is killed, when L-002's failure output contains the literal 'topLevel.final' failure line
criteria.how: In the real run the harness matched exactly the topLevel.final FAIL line, with reading/bytes/files set aside by MayFail, and the Expect 'False'. The real compile-error and crash variants, which have no topLevel.final line, were counted not killed.

criteria.criterion: 6. run the full mutant suite as normally scheduled, when -Mutant All is invoked
criteria.how: -Mutant All exits 0 in 333 s, with EndingObeysSkip among the 9 killed. C-006 confirms the roster matches the ValidateSet. The roster is still a hard-coded list (build-slice's own open item).

criteria.criterion: 7. kill the mutant end-to-end through the standing harness path: the mutated app actually built and L-002 actually run, not hand-patched
criteria.how: The standalone run showed 'publishing the app (eng/dotnet.ps1 publish)' in the scratch copy, then L-002 FAILED on final 'False'. This happened again inside -Mutant All and inside the concurrent C-007 run.

criteria.criterion: 8. confirm the kill comes from the mutation, not a pre-existing failure: L-002 against the unmutated build, through the harness's own sandbox
criteria.how: C-008 exits 0: New-Scratch copy identical to the real source, Invoke-ScratchCase L-002 PASSED with the skip armed and final held, copy removed. The harness never 'restores' in place; it throws scratch copies away. The real source hash was unchanged after every run.

criteria.criterion: 9. distinguish a genuine kill from a broken mutation (compile error or app crash)
criteria.how: Two real broken mutations went through the real Test-CaseMutant. The compile error (CS0103, publish failed) was NOT killed, and so was the crash at the ending (exit code FAIL, no report). The synthetic shapes in C-005 agree.

obligations.evidence: Ran WindowMutants.ps1 -Mutant EndingObeysSkip for real: exit 0, and Test-CaseMutant matched '  FAIL  topLevel.final against core (the ending showed the final snapshot)' with actual 'False'. Build failure versus kill: a real CS0103 compile-error mutation gave 'publish failed with exit 1', no FAILED: L-002, and was counted NOT killed. A real crash-at-ending mutation gave FAIL exit code and FAIL a report was written, got 2 non-matching failures, and was counted NOT killed. A missing report was covered by the crash variant, which wrote none.

Owed to build-slice, not done. tests/bugs/SL-064-MutantCases.ps1 Test-C007 still takes $scratches = Get-Scratches (line 354) and compares it with a second listing of the shared %TEMP%\fsa-window-mutants (lines 367-368). It does not take its own copy's path from its output. Reproduced today with a natural trigger: C-008 started 10 s after C-007. C-007 exited 1 on 'FAIL the scratch copy was removed (…\a5879e2ed00a467c976b0ebd874477ff)', which is C-008's copy (7 mentions in C-008's output, none in C-007's), while C-007's own copy cb024f63… had been removed. Build-slice should apply the fix O-011 describes: match fsa-window-mutants\([0-9a-f]{32})\ in $lines, require exactly one, Test-Path it false, and drop the before/after listing.

not_reached: Kill reliability over many runs: I saw 4 real kills (standalone, -Mutant All, the concurrent C-007, and one control pass). The 20/20 plus 10/10 rate comes from the risk spike's hand-patch, not from repeated runs through the harness.
A killed mutant run with the whole machine under load (except one C-007 run while C-008 was publishing).
Running the harness under Windows PowerShell 5.1: both scripts were only parsed there. All runs used pwsh 7.
A machine with a machine-wide .NET 10 SDK: every run used the worktree's repo-local .dotnet 10.0.401 (Q-003), and each worktree installs its own copy of about 300 MB.
A real mutation that exits 0 without writing a report, without crashing. Only C-005's synthetic shapes and the crash variant, which also wrote no report, cover a missing report.
Future drift: the -Mutant All roster is hard-coded, so a later mutant added to the ValidateSet but not to All is caught only if someone re-runs C-006.
The bug report was only a title. Its intent (a standing mutant in WindowMutants.ps1, no app change) was assumed from the repro test and the design. Nobody confirmed it.
